articleTitle: U-Shaped Terahertz Microstrip Patch Antenna for 6G Future Communications
abstract: In this article a terahertz antenna has been proposed which is designed on Rogers RO3010 substrate, with a standard thickness $10\mu\mathrm{m}$ having relative dielectric constant ($\mathcal{E r}$) $=11.2$ and thermal conductivity of $0.66\mathrm{~W}/\mathrm{K}/\mathrm{m}$. A dielectric material with a high epsilon value is used, the effective wavelength of the electromagnetic wave is reduced within the material, resulting in a reduction of the physical size of the antenna. The designed antenna is compact light weight and is fed using a microstrip line feeding technique which provides ease of integration inside the device. The resonating frequency of the designed antenna is 0.854THz with a return loss $-19.5\mathrm{~dB}$ offering a high bandwidth of 44GHz. High bandwidth application of the future communication requirements is achieved by the modelled antenna.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of a Near-Field Measurement Probe for a Minimized Scattering Cross Section
abstract: This paper studies the relation between the mono-static scattering cross section (SCS) of a near-field measurement probe and its antenna capabilities, e.g. the return loss (S11), radiation pattern and peak gain. For this purpose, a highly parameterized model is created and several simulations are conducted with a rectangular open ended waveguide (OEWG), to assess the effects of polarization and geometry. Different techniques are used to reduce the SCS, while maintaining a high antenna performance. The first one is to reduce the aperture of the antenna, by reducing the taper opening of the OEWG. Furthermore, the effects of dielectric loading and adding absorber material around the OEWG are analyzed. The employed techniques are assessed based on their capability to reduce the SCS of the measurement probe, while maintaining the antenna performance. It is shown, that the polarization is significantly more important than geometrical variations with differences between 3 to 15 dBsm for co-polar and cross-polar cases. An SCS reduction of around 10 dBsm can be achieved, by combining the different techniques, employed in this paper. The advantages and disadvantages of these techniques are described and a guideline to reduce the SCS of OEWGs is presented.

articleTitle: Secure IoT Entrance Using Mobile Application
abstract: The impact of cyber security attacks increased globally, implementing proper security standards to protect data in the cyber environment has been prioritized, while assets are also at risk of being exploited through physical security breaches. Considering the potential risk of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) cards being lost or stolen, third parties can effortlessly gain the privileges of an authorized person. In this paper, we propose a design for a secure access control system that operates on an Android phone with multi-factor authentication to enable secure access control systems. For this purpose, the authorized users are registered in a database that can be accessed by the access control system when the user authenticates his$\backslash$her credentials with a login/password as well as biometric data from his$\backslash$her smartphone. This system works when the user is 10 meters away from the access control system, after that the user will be asked to submit his$\backslash$her biometric credentials. The database then compares the user’s keys and grants access if authentication is successful. This design is intended to reduce the number of cases in which unauthorized access to a restricted area. The observed results clearly meet the required security of physical access control systems.

articleTitle: Design of Planar Ultra Wideband Antenna with C-Shaped Slot for Band Notched Characteristics
abstract: We propose an ultrawideband (UWB) conventional coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed antenna with 1.575 GHz band notched characteristics. To provide bad-rejection functionality at 1.575GHz, it comprises of a C-shaped slot on the radiating patch. The proposed antenna is successfully constructed, simulated, and tested, displaying matching impedance, consistent radiation patterns, and constant gain. To describe the single band-notched UWB antenna’s mechanism, an analogous circuit model of the proposed antenna is shown.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Reduction in Coupled Microstrip Lines using Interdigital Split on Reference Plane
abstract: The proximity of microstrip lines in compact and dense designs leads to unwanted electromagnetic coupling, resulting in crosstalk that needs to be minimized. Various methods have been explored in the literature, including via fencing, guard trace, guard trace with via, serpentine guard trace, serpentine guard trace with vias, and serpentine microstrip lines. However, these approaches often necessitate additional spacing between the microstrip lines, difficult to fabricate, and offer limited crosstalk reduction. Hence, we propose a planar interdigital split consisting of conductive strips, arranged in a fashion similar to interdigital capacitor, and are incorporated within the space available on reference plane between the coupled microstrip lines. That is, no additional space between the lines is required for crosstalk reduction. Electromagnetic simulations are conducted using a 75x45mm RO4003 Rogers PCB within the frequency range of 1-8GHz. The results shows a significant improvement of 19dB compared to utilizing a solid ground on the reference plane. Moreover, the efficacy of the proposed interdigital split approach is reinforced by meticulous parametric analyses. These analyses can assist designers in fine-tuning the interdigital split parameters to achieve crosstalk minimization at specific frequencies.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of X Band Frequency Selective Surface
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces (FSS) have gained significant attention in recent years due to their potential applications in modern electromagnetic and communication systems. This paper presents the design, analysis and manufacturing of an X-band band stop FSS. The X-band, spanning frequencies from 8 to 12 GHz, holds an important place in radar and satellite communication systems The proposed FSS design, characterized by a square patch with a central circular hole, offers selective signal attenuation in this range. Glass fiber fabric is used as a substrate, providing a lightweight integration into aerospace structures and offering cost-effectiveness. Through a combination of theoretical modelling and simulation results, the paper validates the band stop characteristics of the FSS. Furthermore, the proposed FSS is fabricated using the photo lithography method, the measurement results shows that it can provide-45 dB insertion loss at resonance frequency.

articleTitle: A novel avalanche pulse generator circuit with controllable pulse properties
abstract: In this paper, some modifications are done to the fundamental avalanche pulse generator circuit to have control over the pulse width and amplitude. The output pulse characteristics are regulated in two ways: one by injecting a signal with variable frequency into the base of the transistor, and the other by altering the value of the effective avalanche capacitance by appropriately using a varactor diode. The results given in this work show that avalanche capacitance is proportional to pulse width and the injected signal frequency can change the output amplitude. As a result, output pulse amplitude and pulse width can be tuned. Overall, the properties demonstrated by the experimental circuit topologies are applicable to ground-penetrating radar and ultra-wideband communication systems.

articleTitle: Design and Simulations of Dielectric Slabs With Optimal Deformations Using Surface Integral Equations and Genetic Algorithms
abstract: We present efficient and accurate optimizations of three-dimensional dielectric slabs for desired scattering properties. Optimizations are performed by using an effective combination of genetic algorithms and the multilevel fast multi-pole algorithm. A multigrid approach with Bezier surfaces is employed to obtain superior designs that can be fabricated via 3D printers. By simultaneously optimizing top and bottom surfaces, scattering properties can be designed in accordance with the given constraints. Numerical results show that slabs with interesting scattering characteristics can be obtained via the developed optimization environment.

articleTitle: Placement Analysis of Isoflux Pattern Corrugated Horn Antenna on a Earth Observation Satellite Platform for LEO Altitude
abstract: In this study, a concentric corrugated horn antenna on Electro-Optical earth observation satellites and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellites operating in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) is designed and a placement analysis of this design is performed on a symbolic satellite platform in X-band. The analyzes were carried out in the free-space environment of the antenna in CST in time domain. Antenna placement analyzes on the platform were performed in Asymptotic Solver in CST Studio Suite and in Shooting Bouncing Rays-SBR in FEKO. Finally, the obtained results were evaluated and the two analysis programs were compared.

articleTitle: Analysis of Return Path Discontinuity and Use of Stiching Capacitor in Printed Circuit Boards
abstract: When a current reaches the sink from the source, it will definitely return. All electrical and electronics engineers know Kirchhoff’s current law. Kirchhoff’s current law states that the current entering a node must equal the current leaving the node. In other words, the algebraic sum of all currents entering and leaving a node must be zero. Considering this law, it implies that the current must return to its source regardless of the circuit. This current is called the return current.

articleTitle: Analysis and Comparison of Lightning Indirect Effects in Aluminum, Composite Fiber Reinforced Plastic and Expanded Copper Foil embedded CFRP Aircraft with EMA3D
abstract: In this article, the responses of the aircraft structural fuselage (skin) produced with Aluminum, Composite Fiber Reinforced Plastic (CFRP) and Expanded Copper Foil (ECF) embedded CFRP materials to the Lightning Indirect Effect (LIE), that is, the currents induced on the cables, are analyzed. As a result of the analysis, the differences between the current levels induced by the Lightning Indirect Effect on the cables routed inside the aircraft were examined. The LIE on CFRP and ECF embedded CFRP fuselage was compared. The currents induced on shielded and non-shielded cables are compared. In addition, the currents induced on cables of different size (diameter) on the same line will be compared.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of RF Cables During Emission Tests
abstract: Every electronic system emits electromagnetic emission to the environment. These electromagnetic emissions may contribute interference to other systems in the environment. These emissions may occur through a cable (conducted) or air (radiated). At this point, requirements of electromagnetic emission occurs. The requirements say that emission levels should be measured and checked. Basically, test setups include antenna, cable and receiver during radiated emisson measurements. On the other hand, test setups include cable and receiver during conducted emission measurements. Cables are common factor for both measurements and insertion loss of cables may effect all emissions. This is highly important in either case. In this paper, effect of cables are investigated related with emission tests.

articleTitle: Polarization and angle-of-incidence insensitive, single-layer FSS for RCS reduction
abstract: This paper demonstrates a unit cell single-layer Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) layer for sandwich radomes for filtering X-band operations with a center frequency of 10 GHz having a bandwidth of 3.45GHz. The design was optimized as having a 7x7 array size to mimic the unit cell model accurately. The structure is evaluated for TE and TM polarizations for different angles of incidence values having a step size of 1°. A sample radome for a fighter nose is considered as it is covered by the proposed structure FSS and compared with the radome fully PEC material on its surface. Results showed that the FSS implemented version has good agreement with the results of the PEC radome design. Comparisons are also presented in the results.

articleTitle: Near-End and Far-End Coupling Investigations of Conductive Fiber Transmission Lines (TLs) on an Ultrathin Denim Substrate
abstract: An experimental validation is carried out in this research to investigate the potential uses of a conductive fabric as a Transmission Line (TL) for the feed networks of wearable antenna arrays utilized in biomedical wearable applications. Initially, a 50$\Omega$ conductive fabric microstrip transmission line with a 100 mm length was manufactured on a 0.7 mm denim substrate. The wave propagation properties of the prototype were measured and compared to the propagation properties of an ideal copper-based 50 $\Omega$ TL. The results showed that conductive fabric-based TL supports wave propagation properties similar to that of copper-based TL from 500 MHz – 10 GHz. However, conductive fabric-based TL experiences losses at higher frequencies due to lower conductivity and large surface roughness. Afterward, for the undesired mutual coupling investigations in the feed network, a parallel TL with a separation of 6.0 mm was then manufactured and tested. Overall, the near-end and far-end coupling investigations show that coupled conductive fabric-based TLs provide isolation in a manner similar to that of ideal copper-based TL. The results also show that conductive fabric-based TL is more immune to coupling at high frequencies thus useful for most demanding conformal applications.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Beam Splitters Based on Near-Zero-Index Materials
abstract: We present design and simulations of electromagnetic beam splitters that are based on near-zero-index (NZI) materials. NZI structures are metamaterials that possess near-zero relative permittivity and/or permeability values, which can be realized by periodically arranging unit cells. Due to their exotic properties, they may be used to forward beams in desired directions when their geometries are properly designed. We consider homogenized models, where relative permittivity and permeability values are assumed to be small, in an efficient and accurate simulation environment. The results show that relatively simple geometries can be used to re-direct beams, whereas receiving incoming fields with minimum reflection seems to be a major challenge.

articleTitle: A novel technique of pulse shortening through spectral enhancement
abstract: For many years, pulse generators used in communications, radar, imaging, and remote-sensing systems have been requesting advancements in short-pulse generation. For that, the primary objective of this paper is to present a novel technique for pulse creation having a short pulse width and high bandwidth. This simple and efficient pulse generation technique uses two non-linear elements (BJTs) driven by two identical Gaussian-shaped pulses. To extend the spectrum of the output pulse, the pulse generator circuit makes use of the mixing effect inherent in transistors. In comparison to each of the identical driving pulses coupled to transistors, the output signal generated has a wider bandwidth and narrower pulse width. This technique can alter the way of bandwidth enhancement studies in radar, imaging systems, and communication systems.

articleTitle: Shielding Effectiveness Analysis of Aluminum, CFRP, Expanded Copper Foil (ECF) Fuselage and Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) Materials with EMA3D Against HIRF in Aircraft
abstract: In this article, the protection provided by the fuselage of the F16 fighter aircraft model by exposing it to High Intensity Radiated Field (HIRF) is analyzed. In this study, Aluminum, Composite Fiber Reinforced Plastic (CFRP) and CFRP material protected with Expanded Copper Foil (ECF) was defined for the aircraft fuselage and the protection provided by these materials was compared with the analysis. In addition, in aircraft electric fields were simulated. The currents induced in the cables inside the fuselage of the aircraft exposed to HIRF and the spectrum of these currents were analyzed. Finally, Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) material was defined to Canopy to provide protection against HIRF and its protection levels were examined.

articleTitle: Fast and Efficient Near to Far Field Transformation for FDTD
abstract: Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method provides electric and magnetic fields in the near zone of the target scatterer. However, if the focus of the problem is the calculation of the radar cross section of the target scatterer, near field data is not sufficient, far field electric or magnetic field data is needed to be calculated. Near field data could be converted to far field data, but it becomes time consuming as the dimensions of the target scatterer get electrically larger. In this paper, near to far field transformation algorithm is accelerated with a parallelization method based on Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) in order to calculate radar cross section of electrically large targets fast and efficiently. The parallelized method is tested on a sphere model for the verification and time comparison is made between new and classical method for electrically large aircraft model.

articleTitle: Wideband Conformal Meandered Bowtie Antenna for Capsule Endoscopy Systems
abstract: This article presents a wideband conformal meandered bowtie antenna for capsule endoscopy systems for gastrointestinal tract monitoring. The antenna has an operational bandwidth of 0.39-1.06 GHz (92%) and can operate in the frequency band of medical implant communication systems (i.e. 401-406MHz), as well as ISM bands (433.05-434.79 MHz and 902-928MHz). A biocompatible superstrate is also considered to prevent direct contact between radiating elements and biological tissues. The radiation efficiency of the proposed antenna exceeds 90% over the operational spectrum. The proposed antenna also has a stable omnidirectional radiation pattern, enabling a reliable wireless communication connection during the monitoring process.

articleTitle: Active Dual Band Frequency Selective Surface for 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi 6E
abstract: Frequency selective surfaces are essential components to future smart city and smart building network infrastructure, allowing for range extension via reflective surfaces, security of sensitive communications, and interference management between adjacent access points. In this paper, an active dual band bandstop for the 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi and Wi-Fi6E bands controlled by DC bias is presented with design and simulated data. The presented structure is designed to be integrated into large buildings for Wi-Fi management and incorporates signal polarization variations due to mounting location. The direction of the DC bias determines which band, or band portion, of the two Wi-Fi signals is blocked in the vertical polarization and controls the selection in the Wi-Fi6E band for horizontal polarization.

articleTitle: Antenna Gain and Factor Extraction of EMC Test Antennas by Two- and Three-Antenna Measurement Methods in a Comparative Manner
abstract: The two and three-antenna measurement methods are well-known techniques for characterizing the antenna gain and antenna factor and are often utilized for calibrating the test antennas. This paper presents the antenna gain and antenna factor extractions of horn-type EMC test antennas from both two and three-antenna measurement results. Three same-type horn antennas, operating up to 18 GHz, are measured in three different combinations as pairs. The antenna gains and antenna factors are first extracted from each pair (two-antenna) measurements separately and then also extracted simultaneously from all three measurement combinations (three-antenna). Extracted results show that the antenna’s identicalness is a necessity to achieve accurate results in two-antenna measurement results, while the three-antenna method does not rely on the identicalness of the three antennas.

articleTitle: Antenna compatibility of a single layer-FSS radome design for filtering sub-X-band applications
abstract: This paper demonstrates a single-layer polarization-independent Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) layer for sandwich radomes for filtering sub-X-band applications. Thermal plastic-based FSS performed a power loss of below 1% while filtering the band having a center frequency of 6.69 GHz with a bandwidth of 4.3 GHz. To demonstrate the impact of the radome FSS on the antenna performance, an array antenna operating at an X-band having a center frequency of 10GHz presented providing gain of 14 dBi is presented. The results of the single antenna array and the FSS-loaded configuration are compared and the results are presented for different polarization angles.

articleTitle: Dielectric Characterization of Ultrathin Softwear Flexible Substrates Intended for Wearable Biomedical Applications
abstract: In this paper, dielectric properties of low-cost and ultrathin flexible materials are accurately determined over frequency range from 1.0 GHz – 12.0 GHz. In particular, four substrate samples of cotton, jeans, Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS), and silicone rubber (Ak-Sil T1310) owing to their flexibility and robustness are considered in this study. The dielectric constant ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}^{\prime}$) and loss factor ($\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}^{^{\prime\prime}}$) of these samples are extracted using microstrip resonator method and X-band rectangular waveguide method. The accuracy of the applied techniques for the dielectric characterization is confirmed by measuring the dielectric properties of a commercially available FR4 substrate using the same employed methods. The average dielectric constant values of 1.80, 168, 2.87, 2.70 for 0.4 mm thick cotton, 0.6 mm jeans, 1 mm PDMS, 1 mm Sk-Sil T1310 substrates, respectively are achieved in this study. The results demonstrated the use of such softwear materials in effective modeling of wearable biomedical antennas, frequency selective surfaces, and conformal reflectarray antennas.

articleTitle: Hybrid Potential-Field Integral-Equation Formulation for Fast and Accurate Solutions to Electromagnetic Problems Involving Open and Closed Perfectly Conducting Surfaces
abstract: Fast, accurate, and stable solutions to composite objects involving open and closed perfectly conducting surfaces are considered. A novel formulation, called the hybrid potential-field formulation (HPFF), is developed by using potential and field formulations simultaneously. Closed surfaces are formulated with the recently developed combined potential-field formulation, whereas open surfaces are formulated with potential integral equations. The developed formulation does not suffer from low-frequency (dense-discretization) breakdowns or internal-resonance problems. Superior performances of HPFF are demonstrated on canonical problems.

articleTitle: A new Class of MRR Structure based on Edge-Coupled Ring Resonators
abstract: A new class of multilayer ring resonators (MRR) structure is introduced based on edge-coupled ring resonators. Two similar MRR configurations, known as forward-coupling and reverse-coupling, are realized using this new prototype. It is shown that the same characteristics as multilayer rings can be achieved by edge-coupled rings. Second-order and third order bandpass filters are investigated. Both microstrip and stripline structure are studied. This study shows edge-coupled ring resonators behave similarly to MRRs.

articleTitle: Performance Assessment of Different Cable Shield Terminations Under Electromagnetic Field Coupling
abstract: Shielded cables are used to protect the equipment from outside electromagnetic interference (EMI). The integrity of shielding is of paramount importance to obtain maximum performance from these cables. On the other hand, different types of cable shield terminations are preferred without rational in practical applications. This study aims to measure and compare the performance of different cable shield termination configurations under electromagnetic coupling. For this purpose, a test setup constructed around a stripline has been used. The test setup has been validated through both the simulation and measurement. Moreover, to verify the test setup, RF (Radio Frequency) cables and connector sets have been used as a golden reference. After obtaining the expected values from the test setup in accordance with the shielding termination tests of the RF cables, tests were carried out on a military grade cable/connector set with different shield termination configurations. The results show the importance of 360 degree shield terminations at both sides.

articleTitle: Analysis of External Effects of Conducted Emission Measurement with Current Probe Method According to CISPR 14-1
abstract: This paper presents the measurement method of conducted emission on signal lines with current probe according to Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standards which are CISPR 32, CISPR 14-1, CISPR 16-2-1, and other similar standards. CISPR 14-1 gives the limitation of emission tests which have to be applied to the household appliances, electric tools and similar apparatus. In addition, the CISPR 16-2-1 standard addresses the conducted emission measurement methods in CISPR 14-1. The current probe method is one of the conducted disturbances measurement methods mentioned in these standards. This method is an extensive method used in EMC to measure conducted disturbances on signal lines of auxiliary equipment. The main purpose of this study is to examine the effect of noise emitted by interconnection lines and also examine the effect of disturbance current measurement depending on the difference in the inner diameter of the current probe. Furthermore, different test procedures are applied for this purpose. Test results were compared and the method on how to apply the disturbance tests with current probe was presented.

articleTitle: The Effects of Different Mains Frequency Values on Conducted Emission Tests According to CISPR 32
abstract: Conducted emission test is a requirement for all electronic devices operating from mains network. CISPR 32 is an Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) standard which defines all general emission requirements for multimedia equipment. According to CISPR 32, if an equipment is able to operate at more than one mains frequency, performing test will be enough at one of them. However, the design structures of electronic equipment vary with changing mains frequency. This paper presents the necessity of performing conducted emission tests at both mains frequency. Therefore, conducted emission measurements have been investigated for a digital signage monitor and television by using more than one mains frequency without changing the mains voltage in this study.

articleTitle: Examination of the Different Measurement Angles on Radiated Emission Tests of Electronic and Electrical Components According to CISPR 25
abstract: In the last century, with the development of technology, it has been occurred a serious increase in the number of electronic and electrical components used in the vehicles. These components shall comply with some of regulatory obligations in order to use in the vehicles. CISPR 25 is one of the test standard, which is used to evaluate compliance for component and complete vehicle testing. It defines emission test requirements and test methods for electronic/electrical components and complete vehicles. In this study, Radiated Emission test result of electronic and electrical components has been examined whether it has changed or not with different measurement angles. This paper presents the requirement of carrying out Radiated Emission test of electronic and electrical components at different measurement angles. Hence, Radiated Emission Measurements of electronic and electrical components have been taken with using control panel, which are intended to use in the vehicles.

articleTitle: Single Polarized 7 GHz Centered Absorptive Frequency Selective Surface Design
abstract: This paper presents the design and analysis of a single polarized absorptive frequency selective surface. The designed FSS has transmission band centered at 7 GHz with 0.28 dB loss. 1 dB transmission bandwidth is 0.3 GHz. 5 dB absorption band reaches 3.3 GHz and 10 dB absorption band reaches 4.7 GHz.

articleTitle: Systematic Design and Simulation of a Miniaturized Conical Log-Spiral Antenna
abstract: This paper presents a systematic method to design an electrically-small conical log-spiral antenna (CSA). The design is based on a thin flexible printed dielectric substrate to form the cone surface, and then a resistor is added between the spiral arms at the larger diameter end of the antenna. To demonstrate the proposed approach, a 2-arm CSA is designed and simulated. The minimum operating frequency of the CSA is reduced from 1.02 GHz to 0.8 GHz. A microstrip balun is designed to differentially excite the CSA. The final antenna has a fractional impedance bandwidth of 121% (0.8-3.27GHz) with return loss better than 10 dB. The axial ratio of the antenna is also assessed to show its circularly polarized performance within the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Photonic Materials, Architecture, Science, and Engineering
abstract: We review the necessary artistic and scientific fields for the development of any scientific discipline in the history, as well as, in any healthy and contemporary economy. Our case study is photonics, a subfield of electromagnetics, which is undergoing a historical transition from integrated classical photonics to integrated quantum photonics with applications in communication and computation.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Energy Selective Surface to Defend against High-power Signals
abstract: Recently, there is a need for energy selective surface (ESS) using an active frequency selective surface (FSS) to protect communication systems from high-power electromagnetic waves. The ESS structure has a low insertion loss in the operating frequency band according to the ON/OFF characteristics of the switching element, but when strong electromagnetic waves are incident from the outside, the switching element operates to block the operating frequency. In this paper, we designed a unit structure of an ESS structure that selectively passes the 3.5 GHz band in the case of a low-power signal using a PIN diode, and blocks broadband signals above about 10 GHz in the case of a high-power signal. The designed unit structure has stable characteristics up to an incidence angle of 40°.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Virtual Tools for the Visualization of Antenna Radiations and Radiowave Propagation
abstract: Understanding electromagnetics (EM) is essential for EMC Engineers. In addition to learning physics behind mathematics, i.e., Maxwell equations, using virtual tools with the aim of visualization of antenna system radiations, EM scattering and diffraction, as well as radiowave propagation are also essential. Here, simple MATLAB-based virtual tools ArrayGUI and SSPE_GUI are introduced for the visualization of radiation characteristics of basic antennas and their arrays and for the simulation of radiowave propagation.

articleTitle: Optically Transparent Materials for 5G High-Band
abstract: With the introduction of 5G networks in industry and researchers looking towards 6G, the need for dense communication networks in urban areas has incessantly increased. In response, there is an increasing need for antennas that can be placed closely together while being unnoticeable to the public. For these reasons, optically clear antennas (OCA) have been proposed in many works for their ability to be optically transparent while being conductive in the radio frequency spectrum. This work explores the issues presented with OCAs and examines electromagnetic compatibility for higher frequency applications, such as High-Band 5G. A patch antenna array and band-stop frequency selective surface (FSS) for 38GHz are simulated and results are presented that show conductivity issues at higher frequency as a result of shorter wavelengths.

articleTitle: Comparison of Impedance Measurement Methods in LISN Calibration Between 9 kHz – 100 MHz
abstract: This paper contains a comparison of measurement performances of line impedance stabilization network (LISN) calibration setups with different methods in the frequency range between 9 kHz - 100 MHz. Line impedance stabilization networks, also known as artificial main networks (AMN), are radio frequency (RF) instruments used to provide impedance and isolate noise from the power line between VLF (very low frequency) and VHF (very high frequency) ranges. Characterization and statistical evaluation of the measurement performances on impedance measurement, which is one of the measurement parameters performed in the calibration of the LISN device, by comparison between the four methods, was aimed. These methods are setups using a vector network analyzer (VNA) and VNA Tools, which are specified in CISPR 16-1-2 standard, LCR meter, and oscilloscope-current probe devices. Impedance measurements with the methods of LCR meter and oscilloscope setups are based on voltage and current applications. Measurements performed with an oscilloscope and current probe, the impedance magnitude and phase components are obtained with measurements of the voltage and current over the LISN impedance by applying voltage to the system. The methods of measurement, which are performed with VNA are based on the application electromagnetic power to the device under test (DUT) instead of known voltage or current value and, power measurement. These four methods have two different theories, and it is investigated that which measurement method would be more advisable to use in which frequency region of these methods.

articleTitle: Micro-Patch Antenna Design and Frequency Comparison: Efficiency and Performance Analysis
abstract: This research paper provides an analysis of the efficiency and performance of a micro patch antenna design. The paper examines the design of a micro patch antenna, which is a form of a planar antenna. It also investigates the effects of frequency variation on the antenna’s performance. In conclusion, this study provides a comprehensive analysis of the efficiency and performance of a micro patch antenna design and frequency comparison. The results of this research can be used to develop and optimize the antenna for various applications, while also helping to improve its efficiency and performance.

articleTitle: Handwritten Text Recognition using Deep Learning Methods
abstract: Offline handwritten text recognition has been widely utilized in various fields including historical document analysis. Deep learning techniques have demonstrated their effectiveness in digitizing handwritten text as each technique is precisely designed to tackle a specific task or solve a particular problem. In this article, we use convolutional neural network for extracting distinct character features and a recurrent neural network for handling character combinations within sequential data. By combining these models, we create a hybrid deep neural network consisting of three CNN layers followed by a bidirectional LSTM layer. This architecture effectively encodes input images and generates character probability matrices with which the connectionist temporal classification operation computes the loss function. Extensive experimentation with various parameter values allowed us to optimize our model, which we evaluated on the IAM dataset, yielding a reasonably low error rate.
